front_line: Destination-first cruising for the thinking traveler. No kids, no casinos — just curious, affluent grown-ups
thesis: I bought Viking because it owns the one cruise customer few rivals can serve — affluent travelers who pay full fare and prepay a year ahead. The bet is yield-led growth from a real pricing-power brand, not just added ships. I am accepting the risk that net debt, flagged as finance leases only, is far higher than $1.78B. I would sell if the 10-K shows real debt near $8B.
moat: Real brand/habit moat in a narrow niche, but it's a logo unless yield-per-guest is rising — and we can't see that yet.
risks: $1.78B net debt labeled "finance leases only" — true fleet debt could be multiples higher and break the DCF.

lifecycle.open_note: VIking is a premium travel compounder with unusually high forward visibility: affluent customers, strong pricing power, a differentiated brand, and a multi-year fleet expansion that can drive double-digit revenue growth with operating leverage.

drafts.x_post: $VIK is a clean one-number, one-date stock. The whole thesis hangs on real total debt (checkable in the 10-K today) and yield vs. capacity (prints Aug 17). Genuinely differentiated premium brand, but priced above fair value. Dead Simple Score 89. Watching.
video_talking_points: Viking sells premium river, ocean, and expedition cruises to affluent older travelers — no kids, no casinos.
Three banks just initiated positive coverage with Bernstein at $120, and the stock trades at $99 — above the $87 base case.
The bull case: it owns the one cruise customer few rivals can serve, a quiet pricing-power machine if growth comes from yield, not just more ships.
The main risk: net debt is flagged 'finance leases only' — if real fleet debt is $8B+, the base case drops to around $60.
This is a one-number, one-date setup: real total debt is in the 10-K today, and yield vs. capacity prints Aug 17.
Verdict: watch — genuinely differentiated, but you're paying above fair value on a balance sheet the data itself says may be wrong.
